items.prompt:
All cats are animals. Tom is a cat.
So: Tom is an animal.
items.why: Tom belongs to a group that sits inside "animals", so he is one too.

items.prompt:
All birds have feathers. A robin is a bird.
So: A robin has feathers.
items.why: What is true of every bird is true of a robin.

items.prompt:
All fish live in water. A dolphin lives in water.
So: A dolphin is a fish.
items.why: Living in water is not only for fish. A dolphin is a mammal. Sharing a trait doesn't put you in the group.

items.prompt:
All roses are flowers. Some flowers fade quickly.
So: Some roses fade quickly.
items.why: The flowers that fade quickly might not be roses at all.

items.prompt:
No reptiles are mammals. A snake is a reptile.
So: A snake is not a mammal.
items.why: If the two groups never overlap, a member of one can't be in the other.

items.prompt:
If it rains, the street is wet. It rained.
So: The street is wet.
items.why: This is the basic move: the condition happened, so the result follows.

items.prompt:
If it rains, the street is wet. The street is wet.
So: It rained.
items.why: A street can be wet for other reasons: a sprinkler, a burst pipe. The result doesn't prove the cause.

items.prompt:
If it rains, the street is wet. The street is dry.
So: It did not rain.
items.why: If rain always makes it wet, a dry street means no rain. This move is valid.

items.prompt:
If I study, I pass. I did not study.
So: I will not pass.
items.why: You might pass another way. The rule says what studying brings, not that nothing else can.

items.prompt:
All doctors are graduates. Maria is a graduate.
So: Maria is a doctor.
items.why: Many graduates aren't doctors. The rule only runs one way.

items.prompt:
Every square is a rectangle. Every rectangle has four sides.
So: Every square has four sides.
items.why: Chain the groups: squares sit inside rectangles, which sit inside four-sided shapes.

items.prompt:
Some artists are teachers. All teachers are patient.
So: Some artists are patient.
items.why: At least one artist is a teacher, and every teacher is patient, so that artist is patient.

items.prompt:
Some cars are electric. Some electric things are cheap.
So: Some cars are cheap.
items.why: The electric things that are cheap could all be bikes. The two "some" groups need not meet.

items.prompt:
No honest person lies. Some politicians lie.
So: Some politicians are not honest.
items.why: A politician who lies can't be honest, because honest people never lie.

items.prompt:
All members can enter. Sam can enter.
So: Sam is a member.
items.why: Guests, staff and others might be able to enter too.

items.prompt:
If the alarm rings, everyone leaves. Nobody left.
So: The alarm did not ring.
items.why: If ringing always empties the building, nobody leaving means it didn't ring.

items.prompt: "Don't listen to her view on diets. She's not even a size 6."
items.why: It attacks the person instead of the argument.

items.prompt: "Everyone is buying this phone, so it must be the best."
items.why: Lots of people doing something doesn't make it good.

items.prompt: "I met two rude tourists, so tourists are rude."
items.why: Two examples are too few to describe a whole group.

items.prompt: "You're either with us or against us."
items.why: It offers two options when there are more.

items.prompt: "I wore my lucky socks and we won. The socks made us win."
items.why: Coming after something isn't the same as being caused by it.

items.prompt: "If we allow one late homework, soon nobody will hand anything in on time."
items.why: It claims a small step leads to disaster without showing the steps in between.

items.prompt: "The book is true because it says so on page one."
items.why: The conclusion is used as its own proof.

items.prompt: A: "We should spend more on libraries." B: "So you want to cut money from hospitals?"
items.why: B swaps A's point for an easier one to attack.

items.prompt: "Crime rose after the new mayor took office, so the mayor caused it."
items.why: Other things changed too. Timing alone doesn't show cause.

items.prompt: "Of course the council is right. Councils are never wrong about this."
items.why: "Right" is just restated as "never wrong".

items.prompt: "He's a banker, so his idea about climate can't be any good."
items.why: The job is attacked, not the idea.

items.prompt: "Either we ban cars completely or the planet burns."
items.why: There is a whole range between banning everything and doing nothing.

items.prompt:
Kai is heavier than Ivo. Lea is heavier than Kai.
Who is the heaviest?
items.why: Lea > Kai, Kai > Ivo. So Lea is the heaviest.

items.prompt:
Ana is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Dee.
Who is the tallest?
items.why: Ana > Ben, Ben > Dee. So Ana is the tallest.

Who is the heaviest?
items.why: Jo > Cy, Cy > Hana. So Jo is the heaviest.

items.prompt:
Ben is faster than Kai. Ana is faster than Ben.
Who is the fastest?
items.why: Ana > Ben, Ben > Kai. So Ana is the fastest.

items.prompt:
Hana is faster than Lea. Ana is faster than Hana.
Who is the fastest?
items.why: Ana > Hana, Hana > Lea. So Ana is the fastest.

items.prompt:
Dee is older than Cy. Cy is older than Eli.
Who is the oldest?
items.why: Dee > Cy, Cy > Eli. So Dee is the oldest.

items.prompt:
Ivo is heavier than Eli. Eli is heavier than Jo.
Who is the heaviest?
items.why: Ivo > Eli, Eli > Jo. So Ivo is the heaviest.

items.prompt:
Kai is faster than Jo. Jo is faster than Ivo.
Who is the fastest?
items.why: Kai > Jo, Jo > Ivo. So Kai is the fastest.

items.prompt:
Gus is taller than Ana. Ana is taller than Cy. Dee is taller than Gus.
Who is the tallest?
items.why: Dee > Gus, Gus > Ana, Ana > Cy. So Dee is the tallest.

items.prompt:
Cy is heavier than Ana. Ivo is heavier than Eli. Ana is heavier than Ivo.
Who is the lightest?
items.why: Cy > Ana, Ana > Ivo, Ivo > Eli. So Eli is the lightest.

items.prompt:
Hana is taller than Eli. Ivo is taller than Hana. Eli is taller than Cy.
Who is the tallest?
items.why: Ivo > Hana, Hana > Eli, Eli > Cy. So Ivo is the tallest.

items.prompt:
Kai is older than Dee. Ben is older than Cy. Cy is older than Kai.
Who is the youngest?
items.why: Ben > Cy, Cy > Kai, Kai > Dee. So Dee is the youngest.

items.prompt:
Dee is heavier than Jo. Jo is heavier than Cy. Ana is heavier than Dee.
Who is the heaviest?
items.why: Ana > Dee, Dee > Jo, Jo > Cy. So Ana is the heaviest.

items.prompt:
Gus is faster than Fay. Jo is faster than Gus. Fay is faster than Eli.
Who is the slowest?
items.why: Jo > Gus, Gus > Fay, Fay > Eli. So Eli is the slowest.

items.prompt:
Cy is taller than Fay. Fay is taller than Gus. Gus is taller than Dee.
Who is the tallest?
items.why: Cy > Fay, Fay > Gus, Gus > Dee. So Cy is the tallest.

items.prompt:
Fay is heavier than Hana. Jo is heavier than Lea. Lea is heavier than Cy. Hana is heavier than Jo.
Who is the lightest?
items.why: Fay > Hana, Hana > Jo, Jo > Lea, Lea > Cy. So Cy is the lightest.

items.prompt:
Ben is faster than Ivo. Gus is faster than Ben. Jo is faster than Gus. Eli is faster than Jo.
Who is the fastest?
items.why: Eli > Jo, Jo > Gus, Gus > Ben, Ben > Ivo. So Eli is the fastest.

items.prompt:
Ben is taller than Gus. Eli is taller than Ben. Gus is taller than Kai. Kai is taller than Ana.
Who is the shortest?
items.why: Eli > Ben, Ben > Gus, Gus > Kai, Kai > Ana. So Ana is the shortest.

items.prompt:
Ivo is faster than Dee. Dee is faster than Fay. Cy is faster than Ivo. Lea is faster than Cy.
Who is the fastest?
items.why: Lea > Cy, Cy > Ivo, Ivo > Dee, Dee > Fay. So Lea is the fastest.

items.prompt:
Eli is older than Ben. Cy is older than Dee. Ben is older than Hana. Dee is older than Eli.
Who is the youngest?
items.why: Cy > Dee, Dee > Eli, Eli > Ben, Ben > Hana. So Hana is the youngest.

items.prompt:
Hana is older than Dee. Dee is older than Cy. Gus is older than Hana. Cy is older than Fay.
Who is the oldest?
items.why: Gus > Hana, Hana > Dee, Dee > Cy, Cy > Fay. So Gus is the oldest.

items.prompt:
Gus is faster than Lea. Jo is faster than Eli. Lea is faster than Ana. Eli is faster than Gus.
Who is the slowest?
items.why: Jo > Eli, Eli > Gus, Gus > Lea, Lea > Ana. So Ana is the slowest.

items.prompt: Ana says: "Ben and I both lie." Who is telling the truth?
items.why: If Ana told the truth she would be lying, which is impossible. So Ana lies, which means they do not both lie, so Ben tells the truth.

items.prompt: A box holds only red and blue balls. You take out 3 balls and all are red. Which is certain?
options: The box has at least 3 red balls
The box has more red than blue
items.answer: The box has at least 3 red balls
items.why: You held three red ones. Nothing else is guaranteed: the box could be mostly blue.

items.prompt: Mia is in front of Leo in a queue. Leo is in front of Sam. Who is last?
items.why: Mia, then Leo, then Sam.

items.prompt: One of two doors is safe. The sign on door A says: "A or B is safe." The sign on door B says: "Door A is not safe." Exactly one sign is true. Which door is safe?
items.why: Door A's sign is always true, because one of the doors is safe. Exactly one sign is true, so door B's sign is false, which means door A is safe.

items.prompt: Three friends each own a different pet: cat, dog, fish. Ana doesn't own the cat. Ben owns neither the dog nor the cat. Who owns the dog?
items.why: Ben can only have the fish. Ana can't have the cat, so she has the dog. Cy has the cat.

items.prompt: A farmer says: "All my chickens are brown, and some of my animals are chickens." Which must be true?
options: Some of his animals are brown
items.answer: Some of his animals are brown
items.why: At least one animal is a chicken, and every chicken is brown.

items.prompt:
All squares have four sides. This shape is a square.
So: This shape has four sides.
items.why: Being a square comes with four sides, so this shape has them.

items.prompt:
No dogs can fly. Rex is a dog.
So: Rex can't fly.
items.why: If no dog flies, Rex, being a dog, doesn't either.

items.prompt:
All teachers read a lot. Lena reads a lot.
So: Lena is a teacher.
items.why: Many people who aren't teachers read a lot too. The rule only runs one way.

items.prompt:
All apples are fruit. All fruit grows on plants.
So: All apples grow on plants.
items.why: Apples sit inside fruit, and fruit sits inside things that grow on plants.

items.prompt:
If you press the bell, it rings. The bell rang.
So: Someone pressed it.
items.why: A bell can ring for other reasons: wind, a fault, a timer. The result doesn't prove the cause.

items.prompt:
If a number is divisible by 4, it is even. 12 is divisible by 4.
So: 12 is even.
items.why: The condition holds, so the result follows.

items.prompt:
If the shop is open, the lights are on. The lights are off.
So: The shop is not open.
items.why: If open always means lights on, lights off means not open.

items.prompt:
Some birds can't fly. All penguins are birds.
So: Some penguins can't fly.
items.why: The birds that can't fly might be ostriches and kiwis, not penguins. Nothing here links the two groups.

items.prompt:
No cats bark. Some pets are cats.
So: Some pets don't bark.
items.why: At least one pet is a cat, and no cat barks, so that pet doesn't bark.

items.prompt:
Everyone who finishes the race gets a medal. Some runners got a medal.
So: Some runners finished the race.
items.why: Medals might also go to other people, such as the oldest runner or a volunteer. The rule says what finishing brings, not that only finishing brings it.

items.prompt: "You can't trust his sums. He dropped out of school."
items.why: It attacks the person instead of checking the sums.

items.prompt: "It's the best film ever. Everyone I know has seen it."
items.why: How many people watched it doesn't show how good it is.

items.prompt: "My cousin lost weight on this tea, so it works for everyone."
items.why: One person's result can't tell you what happens for everyone.

items.prompt: A: "We should have slightly shorter school days." B: "So you think children shouldn't learn anything?"
items.why: B swaps A's modest point for an extreme one that is easy to attack.

items.prompt: "If we let them build one tower, soon the whole skyline will be ruined."
items.why: It jumps from one small step to a disaster with no steps shown in between.

items.prompt: "This medicine is safe because it isn't dangerous."
items.why: "Safe" and "not dangerous" say the same thing, so nothing has been shown.

items.prompt: "Every morning the rooster crows and then the sun rises. The rooster makes the sun rise."
items.why: Happening first doesn't make it the cause. Both follow the dawn's own timing.

items.prompt: A: "Let's check the data before we decide." B: "So you want to delay the project forever?"
items.why: A asked for one check. B answers an exaggerated version of the point.

items.prompt: Tom is taller than Ria. Ria is taller than Ed. Who is in the middle?
items.why: Tom, then Ria, then Ed. Ria sits between them.

items.prompt: One of three boxes holds a prize. Box 1 is empty. Box 2 is empty. Where is the prize?
items.why: Rule out the empty ones and one box is left.

items.prompt: A is older than B. C is younger than B. D is older than A. Who is the youngest?
items.why: From oldest: D, A, B, C. So C is the youngest.

items.prompt: If today is Monday, the library is closed. The library is open today. What do you know?
items.why: If Monday always means closed, then open means it can't be Monday. It doesn't say which day it is.

items.prompt: Two doors: one is safe. Two guards, one always lies and one always tells the truth. You ask one guard: "What would the other guard say is the safe door?" He points to door A. Which door is safe?
items.why: The truth-teller reports the liar's lie, and the liar lies about the truth-teller's answer. Either way you hear the wrong door, so take the other one.

items.prompt: A shirt and a tie cost $11 together. The shirt costs $10 more than the tie. How much does the tie cost?
items.why: Shirt $10.50 plus tie $0.50 makes $11, and the difference is $10. The quick answer, $1, would make the total $12.
